/direct/extra-fields/http-proxy-no-passw: A proxyPassword field in a direct connect request no longer becomes the saved proxy's password: the proxy comes from the saved settings only (a bug fix; the renderer never sends one).
/direct/extra-fields/*/config: A concurrency field in a direct connect request no longer fixes the size of the transfer pool: the field is gone and the pool is demand-sized, capped by the site's connection limit. With the http proxy, the proxy also has no password, as saved.
/stores/legacy-array-shapes/connect/extr: A concurrency key in a stored site no longer fixes the size of the transfer pool, for the same reason. No version of FTPeach wrote one.
/direct/refused-concurrency/*/refused: A direct connect request's concurrency is no longer read, so a value above 128 is not refused and the connect goes ahead.
/direct/refused-no-host/*/refused/messag: A direct connect is checked by the same code as a saved site's: the refusal keeps its code (invalidInput, which is what the renderer shows by) and says what was wrong in details.
/direct/unknown-protocol/*/unreadable: A request naming an unknown protocol is still unreadable; the reader that saved sites use says so in its own words.
/direct/webdav-url-alias/*/config: A direct connect no longer accepts url as another name for webdavUrl: the renderer never sent it, and a saved site never read it. The connect is refused for want of a WebDAV address.
/stores/*/list/sites/Ok/*/user: sites_list returns a server's fields the way a connect reads them: a user name or host that is missing, null or not text lists as an empty string instead of being passed through. The renderer read both the same way everywhere but two places: the site subtitle, which showed a null host as the text null, and saving a pane as a bookmark, which matched an existing bookmark by strict equality and so did not reuse one whose host or user was null.
/stores/*/list/sites/Ok/*/port: A number stored as a numeric string lists as a number, and one nothing can read lists as unset; connecting to that site is still refused.
/stores/*/list/sites/Ok/*/protocol: A bookmark stored as ftp with secure lists as ftps, the protocol it connects with, so the pane and the editor no longer show it as FTP (B9). A missing protocol lists as ftp, which it connects as; an unknown one lists as ftp too, and connecting to it is still refused.
/stores/*/list/sites/Ok/*/secure: The same: FTPS is always listed as protocol ftps with secure false.
/stores/*/saves/*/filesAfter/sites/data/: A save that leaves the host or user name out stores an empty string instead of null; every version reads both the same.
FTPS is stored as protocol ftps, with secure false, whichever spelling the save was sent in; 0.3.0 reads that form.
/stores/*/import/filesAfter/sites/data/*: The same, for an imported bookmark.
/stores/legacy-array-shapes/saves/2/file: The stored limit a save keeps is written as a number when it was a numeric string.
/stores/*/scopes/*/protocol: A bookmark's password recipient is read the way a connect reads its server: FTPS is one recipient however it was stored, and a missing protocol is FTP.
/stores/current-save-output/saves/4/tran: Moving a saved password from an FTPS bookmark to plain FTP is flagged as less secure (B8).
/stores/legacy-array-shapes/saves/1/tran: Saving a bookmark stored as ftp with secure as ftps is not a move to another server, so it needs no confirmation and goes through (B9).
/stores/legacy-array-shapes/saves/1/file: The same: the save is written, protecting the plaintext password it kept.
/stores/legacy-array-shapes/import/verdi: An exported bookmark is the listed one, so a stored value only a connect would refuse (a numeric-string limit or port, an unknown protocol) now exports as a value import accepts.
